Government Approves New Hydropower Project in Gandaki

By Staff Reporter | Published November 6, 2026

KATHMANDU — In a major development for Nepal's energy sector, the Ministry of Energy has officially approved the construction of a 150-megawatt hydropower project along the Trishuli basin in Gandaki province.

The estimated investment for the project stands at roughly 22 billion Nepali rupees, supported by a consortium of domestic financial institutions and multilateral development partners. Construction is slated to commence before the onset of the next monsoon.

Energy officials stated that the project will significantly stabilize the central transmission grid during dry winter months, when river discharge traditionally drops across Himalayan watersheds. Local community consultations have already concluded satisfactorily.

Power generated from the plant will be evacuated through a 220kV double-circuit transmission line connecting to the national substation at Markichowk.
